rationale: A 29-year-old male presenting with acute diarrhea, eosinophilic ascites, and marked hypereosinophilia. Fecal analysis reported E. histolytica cysts and trophozoites without erythrophagocytosis, molecular PCR, or antigen ELISA discrimination from non-pathogenic commensals (E. dispar/moshkovskii). Colonoscopy and mucosal biopsies demonstrated normal mucosa with eosinophilic infiltration diagnostic of eosinophilic gastroenteritis. In the absence of E1 or E2 confirmation, morphological microscopy represents E3 supportive evidence only -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Parasitoscopic fecal analysis was positive for Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites and cysts, metronidazole plus iodoquinol were initiated.

rationale: A 13-year-old female in rural Cameroon with a 141 mm solitary right hepatic lobe abscess on ultrasound and stool microscopy demonstrating E. histolytica cysts. Due to resource constraints, neither abscess aspiration (anchovy-paste pus), amebic serology, nor PCR was performed. Although the patient recovered following metronidazole therapy, microscopy showing only cysts without erythrophagocytosis or species differentiation represents E3 supportive evidence only, which is insufficient for confirmed VPD -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool exam reveals the presence of Charcot Leydig crystals and E. histolytica cyst.

The results of the abdominal ultrasound revealed a huge heterogenous mass within the right lobe of the liver with thick walls, air bubbles, and a dimension of 141 mm suggestive of amoebic liver abscess (Figure 2).

rationale: A 12-year-old male presenting with bloody diarrhea and acute hepatitis. Stool microscopy noted trophozoite stages of E. histolytica without erythrophagocytosis, PCR, or antigen ELISA discrimination from E. dispar. Video colonoscopy and mucosal biopsy subsequently confirmed schistosomiasis-induced ulcerative colitis with Schistosoma eggs, but no amoebic histopathology. Stool microscopy alone is E3 supportive and insufficient for confirmed VPD -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool Examination revealed ova of S. mansoni and Trophozoite stages of E. histolytica.But the stool antigen examination for H. pylori infection was negative.

rationale: A 31-year-old postpartum female presenting with obstructive jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. Stool microscopy noted non-differentiated E. histolytica/dispar trophozoites without erythrophagocytosis, and ultrasound showed small hepatic lesions that resolved after empirical metronidazole. In the absence of amebic serology, pus aspiration (anchovy-paste fluid), or molecular/antigen testing, morphological microscopy of E. histolytica/dispar is supportive (E3) only and does not establish confirmed VPD -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: trophozoites of E. histolotica/dispar were seen in stool microscopically.
But, there were multiple lesions on the right lobe of liver parenchyma which were most likely small multiple amebic live abscesses.

rationale: An 18-year-old male presenting with intermittent bilateral leg weakness and uncontrolled hypertension due to adrenocortical carcinoma / primary aldosteronism. Amoebiasis is mentioned solely as a past medical history episode 1 year prior to admission ('1 year prior to admission, the patient experienced loose bowel movement and was admitted and diagnosed to have amoebiasis'). There was no active amoebic infection during the current acute episode; temporality is HISTORICAL_PAST and clinical role is PAST_HISTORY -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was again not compliant with his medications and continued to experience intermittent body weakness until, 1 year prior to admission, the patient experienced loose bowel movement and was admitted and diagnosed to have amoebiasis.

rationale: A 4-month-old male infant presenting with vomiting, refusal of feeds, and loose stools. Direct fecal examination using Lugol's iodine and concentration demonstrated cysts and trophozoites morphologically identified as E. histolytica, with occult blood and leukocytes in the stool. However, erythrophagocytosis (ingested RBCs inside trophozoites) was not demonstrated, and no species-specific PCR or antigen ELISA was performed to differentiate Entamoeba histolytica from non-pathogenic Entamoeba dispar/moshkovskii. In the absence of E1 or E2 confirmation, light microscopy morphology represents E3 supportive evidence only, which does not satisfy confirmed Valid Positive Diagnosis (VPD) -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Direct examination of fresh fecal samples using Lugol's iodine solution and the concentration technique showed E. histolytica cysts and trophozoites with red blood cells (occult blood) and many leukocytes (Figure 1).
evidence_items.test_name: Direct fecal microscopy with Lugol's iodine

rationale: A 33-year-old male presenting with acute cholangitis, congenital hepatic fibrosis, and Caroli's disease. Amebic colitis is documented exclusively as a historical episode that occurred and was treated with antibiotics 7 months prior to hospital admission. There was no active amoebiasis during the current acute care episode; temporality is HISTORICAL_PAST and clinical role is PAST_HISTORY -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Seven months before entering our hospital, diarrhea with fever and chills developed. At that time, he was diagnosed with amebic colitis and treated with antibiotics.

rationale: A 62-year-old male presenting with massive pulmonary hemorrhage diagnosed with pulmonary Balantidium coli infection based on wet mount demonstration of large ciliated trophozoites. Entamoeba histolytica is referenced exclusively as an incorrect distractor choice in a multiple-choice clinical challenge quiz; there was no suspicion or evidence of amoebiasis in the patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote:
Q1. On reviewing the video (Video 1), what is your interpretation?
Entamoeba histolytica
Trophozoite of lung fluke
Cyst of Balantidium coli
Trophozoite of Balantidium coli.
The correct answer is

rationale: A 31-year-old male traveler presenting with malaise and diarrhea diagnosed with imported vivax/malariae malaria. Routine stool microscopy noted Entamoeba histolytica, Trichuris trichiura, Endolimax nana, and Blastocystis hominis, for which metronidazole and paromomycin were administered. However, no erythrophagocytosis was demonstrated, and no species-specific PCR or Gal/GalNAc antigen ELISA was performed to differentiate pathogenic E. histolytica from non-pathogenic commensals (E. dispar/moshkovskii). Per CDC/WHO protocol, morphological stool microscopy alone constitutes E3 supportive evidence only and is insufficient for confirmed VPD -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: In a stool specimen, Entamoeba histolytica, Trichiuris trichura, Endolimax nana, and Blastocystis hominis were observed; stool cultures were negative.
metronidazole and paromomycin were administered for the intestinal infestations.

rationale: A 42-year-old female geologist presenting with a cutaneous granulomatous lesion diagnosed histopathologically as lobomycosis (Loboa loboi). Amebic dysentery is mentioned solely as a remote historical travel illness contracted in South America 7-8 years prior to presentation (1993-1994). Temporality is HISTORICAL_PAST and clinical role is PAST_HISTORY without active clinical evaluation or diagnostic claim during the current episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Health problems encountered during her travels included dengue fever, amebic dysentery, and intestinal helminthiasis.

rationale: A 39-year-old female presenting with epigastric pain, weight loss, alopecia, onychodystrophy, and diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis diagnosed with Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. Intestinal amebiasis is mentioned solely as a presumed antecedent episode two months prior treated empirically with metronidazole. In the current clinical presentation, amebiasis is not an active diagnosis or evaluated condition, representing past medical history -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: M. N. is a 39-year-old Filipino woman with a prior history of intestinal amebiasis, who was referred to gastroenterology for evaluation of epigastric pain.

rationale: A 51-year-old male presenting with abdominal discomfort and an 8 x 8 cm ascending colon inflammatory tumor causing obstruction at the hepatic flexure. Stool parasitology examinations showed normal findings, and mucosal biopsies showed nonspecific inflammatory infiltration without identifiable amoebae. Treatment with metronidazole was initiated empirically based on a high index of suspicion of an amebic pseudotumor (ameboma), resulting in rapid clinical recovery and complete radiological disappearance of the tumor. While the clinical and radiological response to metronidazole provides supportive (E3) evidence, microscopic, antigen, or serological confirmation (E1/E2) was absent. E3 evidence alone cannot establish a confirmed Valid Positive Diagnosis -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Parasitology and bacteriology stool examinations showed normal findings.

While awaiting results and with a high index of suspicion of an amebic pseudotumor, treatment was initiated with metronidazole (1500 mg/day). Three days after initiation of treatment, the symptoms disappeared; repeated colonoscopy following the improvement of symptoms showed normal large bowel up to 12 cm in the ileum.
evidence_items.test_name: Empiric metronidazole therapy and clinical response

rationale: A 7-year-old male child presenting with total hypopyon and endophthalmitis following corneal trauma, treated with intracameral voriconazole antifungal therapy. The case report is titled 'Intrastromal injection of voriconazole as a therapeutic of fungal hypopyon' and describes fungal endophthalmitis. The passing mention of 'amoebiasis' in the anterior chamber puncture fluid is a lexical homonym or non-target organism (such as free-living Acanthamoeba keratitis/endophthalmitis) unrelated to human intestinal or invasive Entamoeba histolytica disease -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The puncture fluid being analyzed in the laboratory, revealed the presence of amoebiasis.

rationale: A 55-year-old female presenting with generalized erythroderma diagnosed as erythrodermic psoriasis. Entamoeba histolytica infection is mentioned strictly as a past medical history event recently treated with metronidazole. There was no active amoebiasis during the current acute care episode; temporality is HISTORICAL_PAST and clinical role is PAST_HISTORY without an active clinical claim -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient had a medical history of treated hypertension and was also recently treated for Entamoeba histolytica infection with metronidazole (400 mg, TID) for ten days.

rationale: A 62-year-old female diagnosed with cervical tuberculosis confirmed by acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain. Amoebiasis is mentioned solely in an academic review context listing granulomatous differential diagnoses of the cervix. There is no patient-level claim or clinical suspicion of amoebiasis -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: TB of cervix needs to be differentiated from other granulomatous diseases, for example, lymphogranuloma venereum, sarcoidosis, schistosomiasis, amoebiasis, brucellosis, foreign body granuloma due to suture, crystal or cotton, and carcinoma cervix.

rationale: This publication describes a retrospective multi-patient cohort study evaluating 220 patients with choledocholithiasis and liver abscess undergoing endoscopic sphincterotomy. It does not represent an individual single-patient clinical case report. Furthermore, amebic liver abscess was an explicit study exclusion criterion. Excluded under the Single-Patient / Case-Report requirement -> EXCLUDED_NON_CASE_REPORT.

evidence_items.source_quote: A cohort of patients with choledocholithiasis who underwent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) examination with either endoscopic sphincterotomy (ES) or non-ES procedure (endoscopic papillary balloon dilation) was selected from January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2018. Exclusion criteria included individuals under 18 years old, previous history of ERCP procedure, pyogenic liver abscess, amebic liver abscess, alcoholism, history of hepatopancreaticobiliary system surgery, and malignancies such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), gallbladder and extrahepatic bile duct malignancies, small intestine (including duodenum) malignancies, and pancreatic malignancies.
A total of 220 individuals were confirmed to have liver abscess.

rationale: A 54-year-old male undergoing outpatient treatment for an amebic liver abscess with prolonged oral metronidazole (16 weeks total) and paromomycin, with outpatient fluoroscopic imaging documenting progressive reduction and complete resolution of the abscess cavity. While therapeutic resolution of an abscess with metronidazole and paromomycin strongly supports the clinical episode (E3), this specific CCU paragraph contains only supportive/therapeutic follow-up data without local E1 or E2 diagnostic test results. In accordance with protocol rules, supportive E3 evidence alone -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: Given the size of his abscess and the slow reduction in abscess size and drain output, the decision was made to continue metronidazole until complete resolution of the abscess (16 weeks total).
